title: Radiation embrittlement of fusion structural steels
bottleneck: The structural backbone of blankets and vessels, reduced-activation ferritic-martensitic steels like EUROFER, hardens and embrittles under 14 MeV neutron bombardment, losing fracture toughness over years of exposure. Helium generated by transmutation reactions accumulates at grain boundaries, causing swelling and further embrittlement that fission-reactor data cannot predict. Design codes for these steels under fusion conditions do not yet exist. The gap forces designers to choose between conservative over-engineering that raises costs and aggressive assumptions that regulators reject.
why_it_blocks: If structural materials cannot be licensed for a 5 to 10 year blanket lifetime, replacement frequency and safety-case uncertainty make fusion plants unbankable. Regulators need validated data, not extrapolation.
current_state: Reduced-activation steels are being irradiated in fission reactors and ion-beam facilities as proxies. The fusion-spectrum data needed for licensing awaits IFMIF-DONES, still under construction.

sources.title: Reliable Nuclear Fusion Will Require New Heat- and Radiation-Resilient Materials
